sentences.text: The petitioner and respondent nos.3 and 4 both claim title over the super-structure.
The said issue has been decided by the Competent Authority in purported exercise of powers under the Railways Act, 1989, under which, the acquisition was made.

4. The short submission of counsel for the petitioner is that the dispute relating to the person entitled to compensation has to be referred to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in terms of Section 20-H (4) of the Railways Act, 1989 which reads as follows:-
"20H (4):- If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated."
5. Counsel for respondent Nos.3 and 4 is not in a position to dispute the said proposition of law.

He,
however, submits that the question of title over super-structure has been rightly decided by the Competent Authority.

6. As the parties dispute title in respect of super-structure existing over the acquired land, in our considered opinion, the said dispute ought to have been referred to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction as it falls squarely within the ambit of its jurisdiction in terms of sub-section (4)
of Section 20-H of the Act.
Consequently, the impugned order so far it decides rival claim in respect of title over super-structure is hereby set aside.
7. The respondent No.2 is directed to refer the said dispute to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction for being decided in accordance with law.
The compensation amount paid to respondent nos.3 and 4 for the super-structure shall abide by the decision that shall be taken by the principal civil court of original jurisdiction.

8. The writ petition stands disposed of.
